arxiv-2110-12791.title: Production and validation of scintillating structural components from low-background Poly(ethylene naphthalate)
arxiv-2110-12791.creator: G. Zuzel
arxiv-2110-12791.description: Abstract Poly Ethylene Naphthalate (PEN) is an industrial polymer plastic which is investigated as a low background, transparent, scintillating and wavelength shifting structural material. PEN scintillates in the blue region and has excellent mechanical properties both at room and cryogenic temperatures.

arxiv-2211-13691.title: Open Superstring First Mass Level Effective Lagrangian: Massive Spin- 3 / 2 3/2 Fields in an Electromagnetic Background
arxiv-2211-13691.creator: Karim Benakli, Cassiano A. Daniel, Wenqi Ke
arxiv-2211-13691.description: Abstract We derive fully explicit equations of motion, and the associated set of constraints, describing the propagation in a flat space-time of a charged spin- 3 / 2 3/2 massive state in a constant electromagnetic background. For this purpose, we provide the Lagrangian for the physical fermionic fields in the first massive level of the open superstring.

arxiv-2310-18812.title: UniCat: Crafting a Stronger Fusion Baseline for Multimodal Re-Identification
arxiv-2310-18812.creator: Jennifer Crawford, Haoli Yin, Luke McDermott, Daniel Cummings
arxiv-2310-18812.description: Abstract Multimodal Re-Identification (ReID) is a popular retrieval task that aims to re-identify objects across diverse data streams, prompting many researchers to integrate multiple modalities into a unified representation. While such fusion promises a holistic view, our investigations shed light on potential pitfalls.

arxiv-2403-00825.title: Comparing effectiveness of regularization methods on text classification: Simple and complex model in data shortage situation
arxiv-2403-00825.creator: Jongga Lee closingprice@naver.com, Jaeseung Yim yimyh1231@gmail.com, Seo Hui Park hee30970@naver.com, Changwon Lim clim@cau.ac.kr
arxiv-2403-00825.description: Abstract Text classification is a task of assigning a document into one of predefined class. However it is expensive to acquire enough number of labelled documents, or to label them. In this paper, we study the regularization methods’ effect on various classification models, when only few labelled data is available.

arxiv-2412-09169.title: DECOR: Decomposition and Projection of Text Embeddings for Text-to-Image Customization
arxiv-2412-09169.creator: Geonhui Jang, Jin-Hwa Kim, Yong-Hyun Park, Junho Kim, Gayoung Lee, Yonghyun Jeong, [0.5em] School of Industrial, Management Engineering, Korea University, NAVER AI Lab
arxiv-2412-09169.description: Abstract Text-to-image (T2I) models can effectively capture the content or style of reference images to perform high-quality customization. A representative technique for this is fine-tuning using low-rank adaptations (LoRA), which enables efficient model customization with reference images. However, fine-tuning with a limited number of reference images often leads to overfitting, resulting in issues such as prompt misalignment or content leakage.

arxiv-2510-08932.title: MATT-CTR: Unleashing a Model-Agnostic Test-Time Paradigm for CTR Prediction with Confidence-Guided Inference Paths DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, Ju
arxiv-2510-08932.creator: Moyu Zhang, Yun Chen, Yujun Jin, Jinxin Hu, Yu Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng
arxiv-2510-08932.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Moyu Zhang, Yun Chen, Yujun Jin, Jinxin Hu, Yu Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng. Click-through rate (CTR) prediction models are crucial components of recommender systems, which estimate the probability of a user clicking on an item by modeling the input features interactions. Recently, a growing body of research has focused on either optimizing model architectures to better model feature interactions or refining training objectives to aid parameter learning, thereby achieving better predictive performance.

pmc-12610229.title: Augmented Flow-Induced Outward Remodelling Occurs with Ageing in Mice
pmc-12610229.creator: Bethan Brown, Helen Williams, Samson Egbulonu, Andrew Bond, Jason Johnson, Sarah George, Justyna Fert-Bober
pmc-12610229.description: Outward remodelling of arteries is a feature of cardiovascular pathologies such as atherosclerosis and aneurysm, so a greater understanding of the processes involved in remodelling may aid the development of improved therapies for patients. As ageing increases the risk of atherosclerosis and aneurysmal disease, it was therefore hypothesised that ageing affects arterial remodelling and thereby contributes to these diseases.

pmc-12768694.title: PP75 Empowering Laypeople In Health Technology Assessment Through Gamification: The PARTICIPA SUS/ATS Project
pmc-12768694.creator: Quenia Cristina Dias Morais, Marcelo Goulart, Dominique Spada, Milene Costa, Bruno Barros, Andressa Braga, Marisa Santos
pmc-12768694.description: IntroductionPatient involvement is a cornerstone of the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), legitimizing decisions on the reimbursement of new health technologies. However, the complexity of these processes hinders public engagement. To overcome this, the Participa SUS/ATS project developed a gamified digital platform to educate laypeople about health technology assessment (HTA), empowering them with knowledge to engage effectively in public consultations.

pmc-12770480.title: Insights into de-mixing and morphology modulation in coacervate-membrane interactions from integrating experiments and simulations
pmc-12770480.creator: Sayantan Mondal, Agustín Mangiarotti, Rumiana Dimova, Qiang Cui
pmc-12770480.description: Intrinsically disordered proteins can undergo liquid-liquid phase separation to form condensates or coacervates, which play numerous regulatory roles in the cell. Recently, it was recognized that membrane-adsorbed condensates are crucial for biomolecular localization, and in some cases, induce significant changes in membrane morphology. A detailed understanding of the underlying mechanisms remains incomplete.

pmc-13175686.title: Prognostic Importance of Histomolecular Subtyping of Central Nervous System Gliomas in Low and Middle-Income Countries
pmc-13175686.creator: Altaf Ali Laghari, Mohammad Hamza Bajwa, Ahmed Gilani, Sana Naeem, Sufiyan Sufiyan, Wajiha Amin, Nouman Mughal, Syed Ather Enam
pmc-13175686.description: BackgroundAccess to advanced histomolecular diagnostic testing for central nervous system (CNS) tumors is limited in low and middle-income countries (LMICs), hindering adequate characterization and failure to reach a WHO CNS 2021 diagnosis. LMICs also lack access to targeted therapies, and even conventional chemotherapy and radiation therapies vary between LMICs and high-income countries.

pmc-13221130.title: The molecular profile of gliomas in adolescents and young adults
pmc-13221130.creator: Anthony C Wang, Winson S Ho, Lissa C Baird
pmc-13221130.description: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs), defined as individuals aged 15-39, represent a distinct and underrepresented population in glioma research and clinical care. Gliomas are the most common central nervous system (CNS) tumors in this population and span both pediatric and adult molecular subtypes, making diagnosis and treatment particularly complex.
